_README: Curated laws for ds_contract, merged onto the primitive it names. Absence of an entry means nobody has written the law yet — NOT that anything is permitted. Keep this small: a rule here is a rule an agent will follow, and a stale one is worse than none. Every entry cites where the decision was taken. A key here is a COMPONENT ID — overrides merge onto the inventory walk by id, so an entry named after a token constant (KIOSK_UTILITY_SHEET) merges onto nothing and is law no agent can find. A token's law lives in its docblock, which ds_tokens serves as the `use` sentence on that axis.

ContextualSidebar.useWhen: left sidebar, page sidebar, contextual sidebar, per-page nav, Vercel sidebar, lane door, parent nav vs child nav, back row, views list, sidebar filters, where do a page's views go, outbound sidebar, morph sidebar, sidebar mode, mode switcher, FBA mode, label intake mode, sidebar category heading, hairline divider, sidebar head order, sidebar top layout, where does the back button go, back button below search, find above back, page modes below back button, sidebar header stacking order, chat sidebar, chat threads in the sidebar, recent sessions, new chat button, view-less page panel, exceptions sidebar, exceptions domains, sidebar mode dropdown, page-declared modes
ContextualSidebar.doNot: The contextual sidebar is THE navigation surface for a desk's views (owner 2026-09-28): never add top inline tabs, a header tab row or a segmented view control in the page body instead. Do not list a lane's pages or a page's views in the page map (parent nav) once that lane is a door — no dropdown, no child rows; the lane is ONE row that opens its landing page. Do not put a page's verbs (Sync, Export, Add) in the sidebar — they sit in the desk header, top-right over the list they act on (NavPageActions); the one exception is a VIEW-LESS panel whose recents list IS the sidebar (Chat, `NAV_PAGE_DECLS[...].recentsPanel`), where the verbs ride the `‹` back row as glyph buttons (NavPanelActions, chord keycap on hover). Do not give a page its own sidebar component or row renderer — it DECLARES data (NAV_PAGE_DECLS, the recents surface registry) and the host paints it. Do not add a second search field: the pinned top row is the ONE field (NavFind) on every page — scoped to the page's list on a panel, the ⌘K palette's face elsewhere. Do not paint a page's views as body rows: they live behind the head's view switcher. Do not put saved views or filters behind a menu: they are the body's buttons. Do not reorder the head: the search field is never below `‹`, `‹` is never below the mode switcher, the mode switcher is never below the view switcher, and nothing (views, filters, page verbs) is inserted between them. Do not repeat the account / sign-in footer under every page panel; it lives on the page map.
ContextualSidebar.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/ContextualSidebar.tsx. SIDEBAR HEAD ORDER (operator 2026-09-27, every page panel, top → bottom, all pinned): 1) collapse · THE search field (NavFind: the page's list on a panel with a list — narrows it, grows right over the header while focused, locate pills under it — else the ⌘K everywhere face) — paste-a-list status rides directly right of it; 2) `‹ <Lane/Page>` back row — `‹ <Lane>` on EVERY page of a door lane (a mode never gets a `‹ <Page>` row); 3) the MODE switcher (NavModeSwitcher) on EVERY page of a door lane (Shipping · FBA · Labels & docs; Deliveries · Sourcing), the same card in the same order (door first) with the page itself current — derived by the resolver from lane membership (`LANE_DOORS`, build.ts `modeLaneOf`), never declared per page, pinned by resolve.test 'every mode of a door lane…' (operator 2026-09-28) — OR a page's OWN modes (`NAV_PAGE_DECLS[page].modes`, owner 2026-09-28: Exceptions → Fulfillment · Inventory · Receiving), the same card and renderer via a `<page>.modes` section, the current domain's views under it in the view switcher; NEVER an 'all' mode (owner 2026-09-29: every URL lands on one category, a mode opens its first view) and `‹` stays the local peek (build.ts `pageModeRows`, pinned by resolve.test '/exceptions wears a mode card like Fulfillment…'); 4) the VIEW switcher (NavViewSwitcher). Mode = its own coloured card dropdown (NavModeSwitcher); view = NavSwitcherMenu. Both: HOVER teaches the keys in a card beside the sidebar (never shades the page); CLICK hangs an OVERLAY card under the block (the head never moves; Esc always closes it) with the choices as plain text. PAGE AGNOSTIC (operator 2026-09-27): any page whose desk mounts `DeskPageLayout bare` gets its header from the same NavContext (`useNavDeskHeader`, hydration-safe): the active view as title; with `viewKeys` declared, the title (`To ship ›`, grey bubble on hover) unfolds the views as pills starting right beside it (shortest pointer trip); they STICK after hover-off until Esc, a press outside, or a pill is chosen (NavKeyStrip / NavViewTitle). The body starts BELOW them with what changes often, as buttons: saved views, then filters. A slot that has no data is omitted without reordering the rest; after `‹` (the page map peek) the field stays pinned in the same place. ONE HOST (operator 2026-09-27): it is the desktop sidebar on EVERY page — a page with `rollout: contextual` gets its own panel, every other page (legacy rollout, scan stations) gets the page map with the page lit; never mount MasterNav/DashboardSidebar in the desktop column (it survives only in the phone-width drawer). LANE DOOR pattern (operator 2026-09-27): parent = the page map, one row per lane (`LANE_DOORS` in src/lib/nav/lanes.ts names the landing page; legacy spine SidebarNavList.renderLane and the resolver laneMap both honour it). Child = the contextual sidebar of EVERY page in the lane (the landing page and each other mode alike): pinned head (collapse · the search field, then `‹ <Lane>`), then the MODE switcher (NavModeSwitcher: the lane's pages as modes, door first, the current page lit — Outbound = Shipping · FBA · Labels & docs, Inbound = Deliveries · Sourcing; the resolver emits them as the `<page>.<lane>.modes` section), then the VIEW switcher (NavViewSwitcher: current view's glyph · label · count; the menu lists every view with NAV_VIEW_ICONS glyph, digit key, count). Body: the view's saved views FIRST as one-click preset blocks (Bookmark glyph, lit plate when the URL matches, hover × delete, `Save view` block only while unsaved filters are on; nothing when neither) — pinned at the top as buttons, never behind a menu — then NavFilters: a Sort row (the list's order; queues default to ship-by, soonest first), one row per staff ROLE (Assigned / Picked by / Packer / Tester on queues; Staff / Picked by / Packed by / Tested by on Shipped), one row per date range (Ship by, Ordered; Shipped with a time of day at each end), then the facet rows (closed rows, value chip, Reset pill riding the category hairline — Reset clears filters, never the sort; open options with count 0 sink to the end dimmed unless selected). All of it declared as NavControls (staff[], dateRanges[], sort) in NAV_PAGE_DECLS; every control param must be declared on its route and narrow the facet counts too. Categories are separated by hairlines, never text headings — map and panel alike. Page map order: top rows, lanes, Automations, Scan Stations LAST. Map ↔ contextual swap morphs in DesktopRouteShell (directional blur-slide, sidebarScopeSwap timing). The server contract (`GET /api/nav/context`) carries all of it, so Tauri gets the same IA. CHAT (operator 2026-09-27): Chat is the FIRST row of the page map and the ⌘K pin. `/ai-chat` is a view-less `recentsPanel` page: head = the search field over Chat's list ('Find chats', desk store, narrows the threads) · `‹ Chat`; `‹ Chat …… [+]` — New chat rides the back row (NavPanelActions, intent `ai-chat:new` registered by the page; hover discloses its ⌘⇧O / Ctrl+Shift+O keycaps — ⌘N is Chrome's new window, never advertised); body = its threads through NavRecentsList (`assistant.sessions`, ⌥1…⌥0 open the first ten). ACCOUNT FOOTER (operator 2026-09-27): the staff account bar (StaffAccountFooter) renders at the PARENT level only — the page map (legacy pages, and a panel's `‹` peek) — never under a page's own contextual panel.

NavFind.useWhen: global search, command K, Ctrl K, ⌘K button, find in this list, F to find, page search, table search in the sidebar, search hotkey, find button position, one search field, search scope, scope chip, search everywhere, merge search bars, two search fields, where is this order, which view holds it, locate pills, search overflow, search wider than the sidebar, paste many order numbers anywhere
NavFind.doNot: A list page's Find is declared once — `NAV_PAGE_DECLS[page].search` — and the header field (bare F) takes it on ANY rollout; never an inline SearchField in the page body. Do not mount a second search field in the sidebar or header — there is ONE (NavFind). Do not paint the scope inside the field (no chip): the view switcher under it already names the list, and the field's width belongs to the operator's words. Do not clip the operator's text to the sidebar: while focused the page field grows RIGHT over the header (FindField overflowRight) — its 32px slot never moves anything. Do not open the palette as the page field is typed into (the list narrows live). Do not count a locate pill with a predicate its list does not use. Do not route scans or identify lookups through the page field — that is the palette's job. Do not write the desk-store Find to the URL. Do not mount a page field in the header while the sidebar is closed: the table bar's Find owns the list then. Do not put the keycap at the far right or after the words.
NavFind.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavFind.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). ONE field, search split by the ANSWER: PAGE = narrow the list on screen (`search.source` desk-store / url-param; bare `F` focuses; FindField overflowRight: while focused the well grows right to max(slot, 28rem) over the header's task/pin keys, z-50, the slot keeps 32px); CONTEXTUAL = where the text lives in the section — `search.locate` declares a locator, `GET /api/nav/locate?locator=&q=` answers per-bucket counts with each bucket list's OWN predicate, painted as pills in the panel under the field (tone dot · label · count, the list on screen pressed in, click = that bucket's href with the text kept as its desk Find), and a pasted list of 2+ numbers becomes the located list (NavBulkList); GLOBAL = the ⌘K palette: 'Search everywhere for “…”' row / ⌘↵ / Ctrl+↵ (openCommandBar({ query, scope: 'everywhere' }), CommandBarOpenDetail in app-events.ts; CommandBar.tsx belongs to the search session). With no list (identify, page map, header) the field is the palette's face (RollingHint 'Search' …, ⌘K keycaps, paste key); a paste of 2+ numbers there is located EVERYWHERE (useLocalBulkList('everywhere')), anything else opens the palette already searching. Order inside the well: glyph → keycap → words (HOTKEY FIRST). HEADER RECEDES (operator 2026-09-27): while a page field is grown (`[data-find-expanded]` in the DOM) every GlobalHeader zone fades to 30%, blurs 3px, scales 0.985 and stops taking the pointer (200ms ease-out, none under reduced motion) — GlobalHeader.tsx, one :root:has() variant, no state plumbing.

FindField.useWhen: find field, search field, search box, search bar, find bar, table search, data table find, find in this list, F to find, search placeholder animation, rolling placeholder, rotating hint text, animated placeholder, hint roll, text switching animation, paste button in search, paste to find, ⌘K face words, hover to reveal what a search does
FindField.doNot: Do not hand-roll a search input with its own draft/debounce, keycap, clear and placeholder — mount FindField. Do not animate a hint on page load or loop it while nobody is looking: it RESTS on its first phrase and rolls only on hover or focus. Do not change the timing outside the preset (0.22s spring, 1.8s hold, 180ms hover intent) — hover-only means brisk but readable. No bounce/overshoot and no blur on the roll. Do not use a native placeholder for the hint. Do not split the hint into per-word animation — the phrase rolls as one line.
FindField.law: src/design-system/components/FindField.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). ONE find well for every list: the sidebar search field in its page scope (NavFind), the global header's field when the sidebar is closed (GlobalHeaderSearch — owner 2026-09-28: never a second Find in the data-table bar), and any future table find. Anatomy left → right: Search glyph · `F` keycap · field · paste key (ClipboardPaste; reads the clipboard through the same paste door as ⌘V) · clear (X, always FAR RIGHT, expanded or not — operator 2026-09-28; shows with text, or with a caller-held pasted list via `onClear`; ONE click clears both the text and the list). At rest the hint is gray and the keycap and paste key are hidden (neither takes room); while looked at (hover / focus) the hint turns black and both show — `findHintTone`, `HoverKeycaps`, `PasteKey`, exported with `findWellClass` so the everywhere face wears the same parts (operator 2026-09-27). Optional `escalate(query)` + `below` (ReactNode) fill a panel hung under the well while it has focus and text (below first, then the 'Search everywhere' row with ⌘↵ keycaps first). Optional `overflowRight`: the well leaves its 32px slot and grows right while focused (focus-within:w-[max(100%,28rem)], z-50) — the operator's words outrank the layout; the slot holds the space so nothing moves. HINT = RollingHint: rests on its first phrase ('Find' / ⌘K 'Search'); while the operator looks at it (pointer over it, or focus — `F`, a click; `useHintActivity`) the later phrases roll top → bottom ONE LINE AT A TIME (operator 2026-09-27: per line, never per word — read in one glance; motionPresence.findHintRoll on the whole phrase: opacity + y inside a soft masked edge, no blur; motionTransition.findHintRoll = critically damped spring, visualDuration 0.22s, bounce 0). Hover intent 180ms (a pointer passing through never rolls), then 1.8s per phrase. Leaving rolls back to the rest phrase; the next look resumes at the phrase after the last one shown. `findHints(label)` = ['Find', the list's 'Find …', 'Paste to find']. NavFind's everywhere face uses the same RollingHint + useHintActivity. Reduced motion keeps the swap, drops slide and blur. Sizes: `sidebar` (6px corner, caption) and `bar` (8px corner, body). TWO JOBS, ONE ROLL (operator 2026-09-27): a field with `escalate` rolls keyed phrases (FindHint { keys, text }) — rest 'Find' → `F` + the list's 'Find …' → `⌘ K` / `Ctrl K` + 'Everywhere' (the escalate row's word; fits the 195px rest well) → 'Paste to find' — keys leading the words and rolling with them, so the separate `F` HoverKeycaps is not painted. The paste key never takes focus on pointerdown (a grown overflowRight well would slide it out from under the click). LOOK (operator 2026-09-27): white well, depth ONLY at the rim (inset hairline + inner edge shade; the middle stays white so black words read), 13px text-role-nav medium ink text-text-default, hint rests text-text-muted and turns text-text-default on look; pointer cursor at rest, text cursor once focused, accent-light selection; SEARCH_WELL_CORNER — soft 12px at rest, firms to the control corner when pressed or focused. No grain until the grain token axis lands (ds_tokens grain). THEMES: the well rim is mixed from its own ink (text-text-default → currentColor), so the edge shade holds in dark mode too.

NavModeSwitcher.useWhen: sidebar mode switcher, page modes, lane modes, Shipping FBA Label intake switch, mode dropdown under the back button, where do a lane's pages go on its landing page, sidebar mode dropdown, page-declared modes, e.g. Exceptions domains (Fulfillment · Inventory · Receiving), a page's own sub-destinations as a dropdown card
NavModeSwitcher.doNot: Do not render modes as rows in the body or above `‹`. Do not give a lane of one reachable page a switcher (one page is no choice). Do not add counts to a LANE mode (a lane's modes are pages); a page's OWN modes (`NAV_PAGE_DECLS[page].modes`) carry their unfiltered count (facet context `<page>.<mode>`), amber when the glyph is `alertCount`. Do not add an 'all' / root mode to a page's own modes (owner 2026-09-29). Do not paint a page's own modes as plain body rows (the deleted NavBodyViews / childLevels shape) — declare `modes` and let this card render them.
NavModeSwitcher.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavModeSwitcher.tsx — its OWN dropdown, never NavSwitcherMenu (operator 2026-09-27). One raised card pinned DIRECTLY BELOW the `‹ <Lane>` back row, above the view switcher (see ContextualSidebar SIDEBAR HEAD ORDER). PARENT tier: the current mode's icon in its mode colour (its `SIDEBAR_PAGE_NAV` entry's `tone`: Shipping blue, FBA purple, Label intake teal), semibold, ⇅. HOVER (mouse, instant): KeyHintPopover beside the column — `[G] then` lead, rows `[S]⌂ Shipping · [F]⌂ FBA · [L]⌂ Label intake`, icons in their mode colours; never shades the page. CLICK / Enter / Space / ↓: an OVERLAY welded to the card — no gap: the card's square bottom and the overlay's square top share ONE hairline (absolute top-[calc(100%+1px)], z-dropdown, opacity fade only — the card keeps its height, nothing below moves) with the OTHER modes only — the current one is the card and is never listed twice; rows share the card's column (icon under icon, label under label), coloured, text only. ↑/↓ move; Esc ALWAYS closes it (window capture, wherever focus is) and refocuses the card if focus was inside; a press outside or a URL change closes it; the card is a LIST_KEY_OWNER. The resolver emits the modes as the `<page>.<lane>.modes` section. PAGE-DECLARED MODES (owner 2026-09-28, Exceptions): a page may declare `modes: { label }` in `NAV_PAGE_DECLS`; the resolver emits `<page>.modes` — each ungrouped child (Fulfillment · Inventory · Receiving, gated by `requiresAny`), its href its FIRST visible view, a secondary line naming its views — and stamps the current one `active`. There is NO 'all' mode (owner 2026-09-29: 'All exceptions is too much within one page' — each category gets its own table and resolver; `/exceptions` redirects every URL to one kind via `exceptionLanding`). This card renders it unchanged: the current mode from `active`, icons/tones from `NAV_VIEW_ICONS['<page>.<mode>']`, counts from `useViewCounts`. `G` letters come from `NAV_PAGE_GO_KEYS` (Exceptions: F · I · R) and are taught on the card's hover.

NavSwitcherMenu.useWhen: sidebar mode switcher, sidebar view switcher, Shipping FBA Label intake switch, Exceptions PO paired Pick list To ship Shipped switch, parent vs child nav, hover to see hotkeys, key hint card, click to expand inline, progressive disclosure of views, 1-9 view keys, G then S, go keys, view count chip, exceptions alert beacon
NavSwitcherMenu.doNot: Do not open a flyout menu to the right on hover — hover only TEACHES (a KeyHintCard, pointer-events-none, never pressed). Do not shade or dim the page on hover: a hover on the way to a click must never flash the screen. Do not paint keys in the click overlay — the keys were already seen on hover. Do not repeat `G` on every mode row: one `[G] then` lead, then `[S]`, `[F]`, `[L]`. Do not pad between a hint row's key and its icon: key far left, flush against the icon (gap-1). Do not paint a digit on a page that does not bind it (the page declares `viewKeys` in NAV_PAGE_DECLS → NavContext.viewKeys). Do not mark the current choice with a check — press it in (NAV_CHOICE_SELECTED_CLASS). Do not derive a view count from the filtered facets query.
NavSwitcherMenu.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavSwitcherMenu.tsx (operator 2026-09-27, dogfood). CHILD tier only — the page VIEW (NavViewSwitcher: hairline block, medium, count chip, ⌄). The PARENT tier has its own card dropdown (NavModeSwitcher); the two never share one. HOVER (mouse, instant): KeyHintPopover beside the sidebar column, top-aligned with the block, popping like the AI chat context ring card (opacity + scale 0.96→1 on aiTransition.morph, origin top-left); rows are HOTKEY FIRST, key flush against icon — `[4]⌂ To ship`. No page shade. The pointer sweeps parent ↔ child and the card follows. CLICK / Enter / Space / ↓: an OVERLAY card welded to the block — no gap: the block's square bottom and the overlay's square top share ONE hairline (absolute top-[calc(100%+1px)], z-dropdown, opacity fade only — same edges as the block, row icons in the block's icon column; the block keeps its height, nothing below moves) with the OTHER views as text rows (icon · label · count) — the current view is the block and is never listed twice, the same rule as the parent card; ↑/↓ move; Esc ALWAYS closes it (window capture) and refocuses the block if focus was inside; a press outside or a URL change closes it; the host is a LIST_KEY_OWNER so the desk's record cursor stands down while focus is inside. Keys fire everywhere: bare 1–9 (NAV_PAGE_DECLS `viewKeys` → NavContext.viewKeys, pressed cap presses in for a beat via go-keys-store) and `G` then letter (NavGoKeys).

NavFilters.useWhen: sidebar filters, triage controls, staff role filter, picked by filter, packer filter, date range filter, ship-by date, order date, shipped time of day, sort in the sidebar, saved views buttons, reset filters
NavFilters.doNot: Do not put what the operator changes often behind a menu. Do not count or Reset the sort — it is view state, not a filter. Do not mark a single choice (sort) with a check. Do not declare a control whose param the list and its facet counts do not both apply. Do not re-declare a control shape per page in the component — declare NavControls in NAV_PAGE_DECLS.
NavFilters.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavFilters.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). The body is buttons, top → bottom: saved views; the Reset hairline (count + Reset clear FILTERS only); Sort (single choice pressed in, NAV_CHOICE_SELECTED_CLASS); one row per staff ROLE (`controls.staff[]`, StageStaffAssignPopover); one row per date range (`controls.dateRanges[]`, DateRangePickerField compact; a range with fromTimeParam/toTimeParam adds HH:mm fields once dates are set); then the facet rows (multi-select checkboxes with counts). Every control param comes from navControlParams(), must be declared on the view's route, and must narrow the list and its facet counts through the same server builder (sqlDeskRefinementClauses / buildPackerLogBaseWhere).

NavGoKeys.useWhen: G then letter, go to shortcut, leader key, sequence shortcut, Linear style navigation keys, G S shipping, G F FBA, G L label intake, jump to a mode, parent level hotkeys, KeyHintPopover, key hint card, hover to see hotkeys, hotkeys on the left, header button hover keys, Add button hover, then press
NavGoKeys.doNot: Do not bind modes to Ctrl/Alt+digit (Chrome on Linux switches tabs; ⌥1…⌥0 are chat recents) or to bare digits (views own 1–9). Do not arm inside a text field, on a key repeat, with ⌘/Ctrl/Alt, or from a scanner burst (< 30ms between keys). Do not offer a letter for a page the staffer lacks `requires` for. Do not cache targets in session state — derive them from the registry. KeyHintPopover (exported here) is THE hover key card: hover TEACHES (lead line in sentence case, rows hotkey first `[S] icon label`, pointer-events-none, never pressed), click LISTS (text rows only, no header row, no keys) — never keys in a HoverTooltip label or a click menu, never a second hint card. `at` = { left, top } beside the sidebar column or { right, top } under a top-right header control (GlobalHeaderAdd, operator 2026-09-27).
NavGoKeys.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavGoKeys.tsx + src/lib/keyboard/go-keys.ts (pure machine, tested) + src/lib/nav/go-keys.ts (NAV_GO_KEYS, per LANE and keyed by letter inside it, so no two modes of one lane share one; owner 2026-09-27: a lane's letters never leak onto another lane, and two lanes may reuse a letter). Tap `G`, release, tap the letter within 1500ms, on a page of that lane: Shipping's lane `G S` Shipping, `G F` FBA, `G L` Label intake; Inbound's `G D` Deliveries, `G S` Sourcing. Off a lane with modes `G` does nothing. Targets are static: getSidebarPageNav(pageId) gated by the page's `requires` permission (the resolver's own gate), Shipping via useLaneDoorHref (last view). Mounted once by ContextualSidebar. While armed the desk header's key strip (NavKeyStrip, between title and verbs) swaps to the current lane's modes (`[S]⌂ Shipping [F]⌂ FBA [L]⌂ Label intake`, each icon in its mode tone like the view pills, no `[G] then` lead — the staffer just pressed it), centred top-middle; nothing shades, dims or outlines the list (owner 2026-09-27: no overlay inside the data table); with no strip on screen (fullscreen, Chat, stations) the same KeyHintPopover sits top-centre under the app header, measured at arm time; Escape / pointerdown / timeout disarm. The `?` and ⌘⇧? / Ctrl+Shift+? cheat sheet (KeyboardShortcutsCheatSheet) lists the go keys and the page's view digits while they are mounted (registerShortcutOverviewGroup).

NavBulkList.useWhen: paste a list, bulk paste, many order numbers, many tracking numbers, vendor list, reconcile deliveries, received vs not received, where do these numbers live, check receipts, bulk lookup in Find, pasted list popout, status chips above the deliveries, paste a list in the global search
NavBulkList.doNot: Do not write a pasted multi-number list into the desk store or the Find text — it becomes `search.locate.param` in the URL (or component state on the everywhere face). Do not give the popout its own lookup or verdict: every row, chip and count comes from ONE locator answer (`useLocatedList` → GET /api/nav/locate), whose bucket membership is the same predicate the bucket's list uses; inbound bucket ids stay the recon statuses (`received` / `not_received`) so the ledger's `?recon=` filter (`filterRowsByRecon`) and the popout agree. Do not special-case a locator in the popout (no `STATUS_FACE`, `RECON_STATUS_LABELS`, `applyInboundLane`): a number in a bucket that is not the list on screen carries a link chip to that bucket's href, narrowed by its desk Find — that is how Exceptions is reached. Do not paint a bucket with a raw hue; ink comes from `NAV_LOCATE_TONE_VAR` (nav-locate-tone.ts) keyed by `NAV_LOCATE_TONES`. Do not round the popout past rounded-sm or give rows a square hover; rows hover as an inset pill. Do not ship a row verb without its keycap in the footer legend.
NavBulkList.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavBulkList.tsx + NavBulkPopout.tsx over `NavLocateResponse` (src/lib/nav/context/schema.ts); ref parsing from src/lib/receiving/reconcile.ts (`parseRefList` / `parseRefInParam` / `serializeRefIn`). Declared per view as `NavSearch.locate` (`{ locator: 'inbound', param: 'ref_in', statusParam: 'recon', facetParam: 'recon_reason' }`, pages.ts → incoming.pipeline, where the paste reconciles, and incoming.docked (Unboxed), where it narrows the Unboxed list server-side; a lane switch drops the paste) and read by `useNavBulkList(locate)` (URL-backed); the global face uses `useLocalBulkList('everywhere')` (component state, no page list, bucket ids `<locator>:<id>`). Find's onPaste: `BulkList.paste(text)` takes 2+ numbers (newline/comma/semicolon/tab, cap 150 = `CHECK_ZOHO_RECEIVED_MAX_INPUTS`) → the list; one number stays a Find; typed `A, B` + Enter too. With no list, the page Find shows a `[⧉] [B]` paste key (bare B) opening an empty paste box in the popout's place (↵ check, ⇧↵ new line) that commits through the same `BulkList.paste`. The list is located in one ask (`useLocatedList` in NavBulkList.tsx over GET /api/nav/locate); an edit or a recheck (R) re-asks only the numbers without an answer in hand. Right of the well: `[›] [B] N` toggle (bare B, ↓ from Find) opens a right-start Popover, rounded-sm, h-8 sort bar (Pasted · [O] Order ID ↑↓ · [S] Status = bucket order, found-nowhere first · copy shown · clear), then a bucket filter row (All N · each bucket with its count · Not found N) writing `statusParam`. Rows: bucket glyph + label chip in the bucket's tone (or Not found) → number (mono) → detail → title → link chips to its other buckets; hover/cursor = inset pill, press sinks 1px; row verbs Open record (when `recordHref`)/Edit/Copy/Remove/Recheck (E · C · ⌫ · R), ⇧C copies every number shown. An optional `locate.facetParam` (inbound: `recon_reason`) narrows to entries whose `facet.id` matches; changing the status drops it. ↵ pinpoints: when a bucket holding the number is the list on screen (href pathname + view params match, or a verdict bucket with no href), the desk Find narrows to it; otherwise it pushes that bucket's href with that pathname's desk Find (`setDeskSearch`) set to the number. Esc returns focus to the toggle. On /incoming the list's STATUSES also sit top-left above the deliveries (`IncomingStatusChips`, ⌥1–⌥N) and write the same `?recon=`, narrowing the ledger AND the popout; with no list those chips are delivery-state buckets writing `?state=`. CopyChip.useWhen: copy chip, last-8, order number, tracking, serial, purchase order, sku, identifier, clipboard, OrderIdChip, TrackingChip, SerialChip, PoChip
CopyChip.doNot: Do not hand-roll a copyable id span. Use the named variant (OrderIdChip, TrackingChip, SerialChip, PoChip, …) when one exists. Tones live in CHIP_TONES — do not invent a hue. Hover menu is CopyChipHoverMenu, not a fork. Not a status chip (that is badge or StatusBadge). TRUNCATION (operator 2026-09-12): abbreviate on a DELIMITER, never at a blind offset. `getLast8` is `raw.slice(-8)`, so `113-1397006-0292212` renders `-0292212` — a leading dash that reads as a negative number or a system error to someone scanning a column at speed, and that makes the column edge jagged because a separator carries different visual weight than a digit. Prefer the last delimiter-bounded segment (`0292212`); fall back to the last 8 characters ONLY when the id has no delimiter; then strip any leading non-alphanumerics from the result. NEVER pad an identifier to a fixed width. `5034` is not `00005034`: staff read these aloud and key them into an RF scanner, and a padded id is a WRONG id. Uniformity comes from right-alignment plus `font-mono tabular-nums` — the right edge is the scanning line — not from falsifying the value. A leading `#` on an order chip is the HashIcon glyph (identifier-class marker), not a truncation artifact: do not strip it.
CopyChip.law: src/components/ui/CopyChip.tsx — CHIP_TONES is the hue SoT; HashIcon is the identifier glyph. src/lib/copy-chip-format.ts — getLast8 / getLast8Serial are the abbreviation SoT. Do not swap the inset for a spacing token — it is the rail's own measurement, used twice.

Law M1 bans layout tweens; transform was struck from that ban 2026-08-25, so the fill is legal only in that form. Duration is motionDuration.progressFill (100ms), never an inline literal. Progression is a COUNT, never a pointer position: pass satisfied-required-steps over total-required, so a pointer sitting on step 5 of 8 does not render 5/8. The `segments` prop is the touch/mobile-first face (operator 2026-09-14): N discrete increments, per-segment scaleX fill of the SAME law, aria progressbar wiring on the wrapper. Do not hand-roll a second segmented bar anywhere — kiosk, /m, or desk.

Do not auto-complete the steps in between. Every step stays mounted from the first frame (existing invariant 1) — that is what makes a jumped-past open step visible without a scroll, so do not virtualize or collapse the list.

calendar.useWhen: calendar, date picker, day picker, month grid, shadcn calendar, 21st.dev calendar, react-day-picker
calendar.doNot: Do not import 'react-day-picker/style.css'. Do not write data-[range-start=true] / data-[range-end=true] / data-[range-middle=true] chains: this repo is on react-day-picker v10, which emits none of those attributes — that is v9, and most shadcn range snippets in circulation are v9 or v8. Do not put raw text-blue-* inside an arbitrary variant ([&>button]: or hover:); the dark-scheme remap in styles/globals.css only rewrites the BARE class, so it goes dark-on-dark — use a themed token. Do not drop relative or w-fit from the root, and do not simplify nav to inset-x-0 top-0: the p-3 root makes those offsets wrong by 12px vertically and 16px horizontally. A relative stamp (“4d”) is not sufficient alone for SLA work — carry the exact timestamp with it. If a surface needs uniform columns, click-to-sort headers and operational fields, it wants the ONE TABLE ENGINE (DataTable), not a restyled list: a read plane is a MOUNT.

Never wrap the slots in px-mode-page or space-y, and never box the card or the door list — full-bleed rows are what later left/right swipe actions attach to. This is the ONE record grammar on /m (the repair hub exoskeleton). Do not hand-roll a hub from ModeRegion + MobileDetailTopBar + cards: mount DetailHubScreen with card = a DetailSummaryCard mapper (whole card → /info), rows = detailDoor(base, id, title, icon, { meta, enabled }) doors from @/lib/mobile/detail-door, dock = DetailDock (≤3 verbs, one primary) — or MobileCaptureWindow when the hub's job is scanning, and put the dock's sheets in children. /info and each job screen mount DetailRecordFrame. Never put a heading above the card, an Edit button or pencil on the hub (the only edit is the /info bar pencil opening a BottomSheet), router.back()/router.push for Back (backHref), a nested <main>, useEffect+fetch for hub facets (React Query, qk.<entity>.hub), a hand-rolled sticky bottom bar, or MobileTriagePage / ItemCardRow / a row → BottomSheet as an entity record. DetailHubScreen.law: src/design-system/components/DetailHubScreen.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-ds-law-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md. DetailSummaryCard.doNot: Full-bleed, no border box and no radius (operator 2026-09-25: edge to edge); the hub draws the rule under it. This is the first, read-only preview of ONE scanned entity — never a dashboard tile, a list-row replacement, or a second editable form. Exactly one full-width title (truncate), at most two job-relevant caption lines, a mono identifier bottom-left and one status chip bottom-right. The ID and chip MUST share box height (transparent border + py-0.5 on the ID; border + py-0.5 on the chip). The WHOLE card opens the entity's /info screen; do not put a pencil, Edit text, status selector, or another button on the card. The ONLY edit pencil is in the /info top bar. Do not put a heading such as Information above the card. It fills the card slot of DetailHubScreen (map an entity onto it, e.g. RepairInfoCard); the hub, not the card, mounts DetailNav doors and the <=3-verb DetailDock. Pick and pack hubs open their existing task runner rather than embedding its steps.
DetailSummaryCard.law: src/design-system/components/DetailSummaryCard.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-entity-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md. Operator 2026-09-24: simple first view; details on tap; status bottom-right; customer phone in the preview; pencil only in the expanded view.

DetailDock.useWhen: mobile entity hub verbs, hub dock, thumb-zone verbs, bottom action dock, edge-to-edge bottom bar, flush verb bar, repair hub actions, SKU exception actions, scanned entity verbs, mobile exoskeleton dock, scan dock, serial scan bottom, scan button, job CTA bar, next unit bar, selection bar, batch action bar, single full-width bottom button, inline verb band, row verbs, take and pass buttons, board row actions, order card actions, 2x2 action grid under a record, scan in the middle of the bottom bar, centred scan button, floating CTA, floating job button over a list, Start picking, fixed-width bottom CTA, CTA with no bar
DetailDock.doNot: At most three verbs and exactly one primary. The bar is FLUSH (operator 2026-09-25: "no padded top, left and right for the buttons, must be edge to edge"): verbs fill the bar edge to edge with square corners and no gap, a 1px border-mode-rule between adjacent verbs, only the safe-area inset below — never wrap it in page padding, re-add a grid gap, or pass rounded-mode to its cells. It is the ONLY surface on a hub that changes the entity: never add verbs to the summary card, the top bar, or the door rows. Do not hand-roll a sticky bottom nav with a Button grid on a hub; that is this component. It is also every phone screen's bottom execution bar (operator 2026-09-25, industrial terminal block): 72px flush cells (min-h-18), instant ink inversion on press (no transition, no scale), a leading-edge 500ms lock so a double-tap fires once, and a press buzz where the Vibration API exists. State 3 — a one-job screen (Next unit, Scan another label) passes ONE verb and it fills the bar; State 2 — a selection passes selection={{ count, onClear }} and a dark 30% dismiss cell (✕ N SEL) leads ≤2 verbs. Never hand-roll a sticky bottom bar for a job CTA or a selection bar; never bring global navigation to the bottom (it lives in MobileSidebarDrawer). Scanning is NOT a dock verb: a screen whose job is scanning (serials into a visit, labels into a queue) mounts MobileCaptureWindow (src/components/mobile/station/MobileCaptureWindow.tsx) as its bottom surface — lens, collapsed Scan bar to re-arm, and its keyed fallback for typing a code by hand — or it has no scan at all. Never a Scan verb that opens the window, never a hand-rolled typed-entry bar beside it (operator 2026-09-25). A verb that NAVIGATES to /m/scan ("Scan again") is not a scanner and stays a verb. INLINE (owner 2026-09-26, pick edge-to-edge): placement="inline" is the same band in-flow under a record (a list row, an order card) — full width with a border-t rule, not sticky, no safe-area pad, up to four verbs (four = flush 2×2, 1px rules both ways), 48px cells whose labels wrap and never truncate. Never hand-roll a padded grid-cols-2 gap-2 of bordered Buttons under a row; that is this. CENTRED SCAN (owner 2026-09-26): on a scanning job screen the camera's collapsed Scan bar is the dock's MIDDLE cell between two verbs, in its success fill for hierarchy — pass it via MobileCaptureWindow collapsedFrame={(scan) => <DetailDock center={scan} …/>}; never a Scan row stacked above the dock, and never a Scan verb of your own. With the lens up, the dock renders alone under the panel. In a TRIAGE region (a phone FORM — /m/orders/new, owner 2026-09-27) the same verbs paint as separate design-system Buttons (radius control, primary / secondary, min-h-mode-hit-cta) on a bg-mode-bar strip padded px-mode-page py-2 with gap-2 — never hard-flush a face in a triage region; the industrial terminal block (and the N SEL selection cell) is unchanged everywhere else. The region decides: read useMode(), never a prop. placement="float" (owner 2026-09-28, /m/pick Start picking) is a LIST screen's job CTA: no bar — NO hairline, NO bg strip; ≤2 xl pill buttons (depth) at ONE fixed centred width (FLOATING_CTA_WIDTH, the same on every phone, never edge to edge), pb-4 + the safe-area inset off the bottom; mount it as the LAST child of the scrolling flex-column list so the list scrolls under it and its flow height is the list's bottom clearance. Never re-add a border-t / bg-mode-bar to it or hand-roll a sticky CTA div.
DetailDock.law: src/design-system/components/DetailDock.tsx · docs/handoff/mobile-entity-exoskeleton-HANDOFF.md (DetailDock, from RepairWorkbenchDock) · docs/handoff/fnsku-reprint-HANDOFF.md (flush bar). KioskCartLineCard.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskCartLineCard.tsx · src/lib/kiosk/cart-card-view.ts · docs/mobile-first/SURFACE_LAW.md §5. Kiosk DS unification Phase 2, 2026-09-14; flattened 2026-09-15 with the sheet.

KioskTicketStep.useWhen: kiosk support ticket choice, link existing ticket on a tablet, create new ticket at the counter, attach a repair drop-off to a helpdesk ticket, kiosk ticket picker, counter ticket candidate list, create-or-link slider under a signature
KioskTicketStep.doNot: NOT its own step, not mounted flat, and not a stacked pill pair. It rides UNDER the signature pad inside Review & sign, revealed by the ink: operator 2026-09-15 asked for it 'after the customer has submitted their signature', then collapsed the fifth step ('because the stepper is full at that review and sign step, would it be best to include a slider … below the signature so it would be mounted under one step?'), then simplified the control ('the create new and the link existing should be simplified into just one slider where you would be able to slide back and forth since this would be on a mobile display, and automatically select create new ticket'). So: ONE sunken pill TRACK holding two KioskChip row halves — the selected half's accent wash is the thumb, the idle half stays transparent because the track is the only sunken plane. CREATE is the position an untouched control shows, which is honest only because `null` also posts as create (kioskTicketWork) and counts as settled (isKioskTicketChoiceSettled); the HALF-FINISHED state — slid to Link with nothing picked — is what still refuses the commit. Do not mount the DESK link surface: TicketPicker / TicketPickRow / DenseComposeSearchInput / SearchableSelectField (ClaimModeSelect) are desk-micro chrome built for a mouse, and a candidate list on a counter tablet is CARDS (SURFACE_LAW §5), the KioskCartLineCard anatomy — hairline + MOBILE_SCAN_ROW_CORNER, title line, facts as KioskChip meta chips. Do not re-implement the search: the debounce / abort / error-mapping / stale-result rules are the shared useTicketSearch, adapted by useKioskTicketSearch (URL + kioskFetchHealed transport are the ONLY kiosk-specific parts) — the same split useClaimTicketSearch made for a carton. The decision is a VISIT fact on the session root (`ticketChoice`), never a cart-line payload field: `ticketWork` is transaction-level and fans out to one outbox row per repair. A picked ticket outlives a re-search (the hook's own `selectedTicket` is unused here) and outranks the ticket-number PROJECTION on the paperwork, because ATTACH_TICKET stamps repair_service.ticket_number with it.
KioskTicketStep.law: src/components/kiosk/KioskTicketStep.tsx · src/components/kiosk/useKioskTicketSearch.ts · src/lib/kiosk/repair-ticket-choice.ts · GET /api/kiosk/repair/ticket-candidates · kiosk-ticket-step.test.ts (7 contracts) + repair-ticket-choice.test.ts (7 behaviours). Operator 2026-09-15. Mounted under the SignaturePad on KioskRepairPane's Review & sign (step 4 of 4); a settled answer is half of repairStepGates[3], the other half being the signature. The form control is KioskEntryField (`src/components/kiosk/KioskEntryField.tsx`), never a raw <input> and never the desk field primitives: KIOSK_POS_ENTRY holds the 16px floor that stops iOS from zooming the whole surface on focus (COUNTER_MIN_FIELD_TEXT_PX). AnchoredLayer.doNot: Do not read facts in a popout and act on them somewhere else: every row's verbs (Edit ✎, Copy, ✕ delete) sit INLINE in that row, on the RECORD_TRAILING_CELL_CLASS axis (Principle 3 — action proximity). Do not navigate the page or replace the list to show this layer — it floats over a frame that stays put (Principle 2 — stable frame). Do not trap focus here (only L4 dialogs trap). Do not hard-code a corner on the panel: it follows the mode (rounded-mode-control) — square on the Floor, rounded in triage. Do not hand-roll a portal + outside-click + Esc: mount this (or the house Popover that wraps it).
AnchoredLayer.law: src/design-system/primitives/AnchoredLayer.tsx (house Popover wraps it). Disclosure ladder: DESIGN_SYSTEM.md. This primitive is L2.
